name: Thematic Coding
title: Thematic Coding
answer: Thematic coding is a qualitative analysis technique for identifying, organising and interpreting patterns of meaning in text, interview transcripts, field notes and other unstructured material. In mixed methods work it often sits alongside quantitative coding to explain survey results or build typologies. AI assisted thematic coding uses language models to suggest candidate codes, cluster similar passages and retrieve supporting quotations, but the researcher remains responsible for naming themes and judging their significance.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: Thematic coding is a qualitative analysis technique for identifying, organising and interpreting patterns of meaning in text, interview transcripts, field notes and other unstructured material. In mixed methods work it often sits alongside quantitative coding to explain survey results or build typologies. AI assisted thematic coding uses language models to suggest candidate codes, cluster similar passages and retrieve supporting quotations, but the researcher remains responsible for naming themes and judging their significance.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The work typically runs on qualitative data analysis software such as NVivo, MAXQDA or ATLAS.ti, often with a local project file or a cloud workspace. AI features may call hosted large language models through an application programming interface, or run smaller open models on the researcher's own machine. The practical requirements are modest: a standard laptop can handle most coding projects, while very large corpora may need more memory or a server.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: A coder usually begins by reading a sample of the data and creating an initial codebook, either inductively from the material or deductively from a research question. Passages are tagged with one or more codes, and codes are then grouped into broader themes through constant comparison. AI tools can speed this up by proposing codes for uncoded text, summarising coded excerpts and checking for inconsistent application of the codebook, but a human coder still reviews every suggested label.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: The main risks are privacy, consent and provenance. Transcripts and field notes often contain personal or sensitive information, so data should be de-identified before any cloud based model sees it, and participants should know how AI will be used. Researchers also need to record which codes were suggested by a model and which were assigned by a person, because the origin of a code can affect the credibility of the analysis. Copyright and licensing matter less for interview data than for published texts, but the same traceability principle applies.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: Thematic coding is moving toward tighter integration between qualitative software and language models, with features for cross language coding, longitudinal theme tracking and mixed methods linkage. Researchers are also developing shared codebooks and evaluation sets so that AI coding can be compared across projects rather than treated as a private black box. The likely outcome is not fully automated analysis but a faster, more auditable workflow in which the human analyst spends more time on interpretation and less on mechanical tagging.
